Rubio: Musk Sets Ukraine’s Starlink Access, Not White House — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said SpaceX and Elon Musk determine Ukraine’s access to Starlink under a private commercial contract. His comments follow reports that Musk ordered restrictions affecting Ukrainian military drones. Kyiv says the limits have weakened its defenses, while conflicting accounts persist over the White House’s involvement and who controls the service.

Russian Ports Lose Up to 100% of Cargo, Seek Government Bailout After Drone Strikes — Russian ports on the Black and Azov seas lost up to 100% of cargo volumes in September following massive drone attacks, prompting officials to seek state bailouts. The disruption has put thousands of jobs at risk and caused estimated monthly losses exceeding $2.2 billion.

Ukrainian Drone Maker Wild Hornets Rethinks Reliance on Starlink — The Ukrainian drone manufacturer Wild Hornets says it is reevaluating its reliance on SpaceX's Starlink system following recent service disruptions. It says it is exploring alternatives for guidance and control that don't rely on a satellite link, with current options ranging from proprietary digital communication to boosted video transmission.

Kremlin Rejects Energy Ceasefire But Says Full Peace Deal Requires Ukraine’s Participation — The Kremlin’s spokesperson said Putin is not considering an energy ceasefire with Ukraine but added that a full resolution of the war requires Ukrainian officials’ participation. Peskov also dismissed recent European peace proposals as unlikely to contribute constructively to a settlement.

Drone Attacks on Cargo Ships in the Black Sea — At least seven merchant ships have reportedly been targeted by drones in the Black Sea near Romania and Bulgaria, raising concerns about escalating tensions and threats to global trade. European media call for protecting grain exports, warn of potential NATO security implications, and debate Russia’s possible involvement. However, the perpetrators remain unconfirmed, with investigations needed before accusations are made.

Kyiv Mayor Klitschko Accuses Government of Staging Anti-Mayor Protest — Klitschko accused Ukraine’s central government of backing calls for his resignation amid criticism of Kyiv’s winter preparations, shelter provision and spending. He offered no direct evidence, framing the protest as part of a broader struggle over control of the capital.

Air Raid Alerts Stall Ukraine-Poland Border Crossings — Air-raid alerts are repeatedly interrupting border clearance between Ukraine and Poland, with freight drivers facing estimated waits of up to 40 hours at Dorohusk. Passenger-vehicle queues at Krakivets and Shehyni eased by the morning of Wednesday, Oct. 21 compared with the previous evening. Customs authorities said repeated security-related stoppages were slowing cross-border traffic.

Witkoff Arrives in St. Petersburg for Putin Talks as US and Ukraine Agree on Peace Proposals — US envoy Witkoff arrived in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21 for talks with Putin on ending Russia’s war against Ukraine. During talks he urged Putin to consider resuming trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US, bringing documents outlining approaches to ending the war. The Kremlin said Putin would review the proposals.

2 Killed as Russian Drone Hits 24-Story Residential Building in Kyiv — A Russian drone struck a 24-story residential building in Kyiv during an overnight attack on Oct. 21, sparking fires and damaging vehicles. Emergency services responded to the scene as authorities assessed the destruction.

Russia Has Up to 700 Ballistic Missiles, 6,200 Attack Drones Ready to Strike Ukraine, Intelligence Says — Russia has stockpiled up to 700 ballistic missiles and more than 6,000 attack drones for strikes against Ukraine, according to Ukrainian intelligence. Moscow is producing around 10,000 drones monthly, expanding its arsenal as it seeks to overwhelm Ukraine’s air defenses.

From Resilience to Resurrection: Ukraine’s Family Businesses and the Next Economic Miracle — Ukraine's entrepreneurial families have learned under fire what most companies never have to learn. The question for the next decade is whether that knowledge becomes the foundation of regional champions, and whether Central and Eastern Europe is ready to build them together.

‘To the Shelter, Quickly!’ Air Raids Reshape Kyiv School Life — Ukrainian schoolchildren abandon toys and rush to shelters as Russian drones strike near their playgrounds. With air raid alerts sounding repeatedly throughout the school day, teachers struggle to reassure frightened pupils and keep lessons going underground.

Musk Ordered Starlink Slowdown That Disrupted Ukrainian Drone Operations – WSJ — Elon Musk ordered restrictions on Starlink’s military-grade service used by Ukraine, disrupting drone strikes and air defense operations, the Wall Street Journal reported. The move exposed Kyiv’s dependence on SpaceX as Ukrainian officials sought to restore connectivity amid worsening relations with Washington.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 20, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on October 20, 2026.

Trump Demands Zelensky ‘Make a Deal’ as Republican Senator Says Putin Is Playing Him ‘Like a Fiddle’ — US President Donald Trump renewed pressure on Volodymyr Zelensky to negotiate a deal with Russia, drawing sharp criticism from Republican Senator Thom Tillis following a bipartisan call with the Ukrainian leader. Tillis warned that Putin was manipulating Trump and questioned delays in approving European Patriot missile transfers to Ukraine. Meanwhile, US officials reported progress in talks wit

Two Killed in Kharkiv Region as Russia Launches Overnight Missile and Drone Attacks Across Ukraine — Russian overnight attacks on Oct. 21 killed two elderly residents in Kharkiv region and affected 11 others, including two children. Strikes also hit Kremenchuk, Kyiv, Mykolaiv and Chernihiv regions. Ukraine reported 98 drones and six missiles launched overnight, with 58 drones intercepted or suppressed.

Sleepless Nights, Drone Attacks and Blackouts – How Kyiv Families Survive Russia’s Relentless Strikes — Russian drone attacks, air raid alerts and power outages are reshaping daily life for families in Ukraine’s capital. AFP follows 44-year-old mother of three Anastasiia Zhmutska as she navigates sleepless nights, disrupted school schedules, dangerous journeys and the constant responsibility of keeping her children safe.

Zelensky Warns of Russia-Iran Nexus as Washington Pursues Moscow Talks — President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia has supplied drones to Iran and likely shared satellite intelligence with Tehran, reinforcing earlier Ukrainian intelligence findings that Moscow helped monitor US military installations in the Middle East. His warning comes as President Donald Trump downplays Russian assistance to Iran while pursuing negotiations with Moscow.

No Talks on Ukraine’s Future Without Kyiv at the Table – Zelensky on Possible Trump-Putin-Xi Meeting — President Volodymyr Zelensky insists Ukraine must be represented in any negotiations concerning its future, responding to discussions of a possible summit between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. Speaking in Oslo, he also reported positive signals from Washington on security guarantees, the restoration of missile early-warning intelligence and further military assistance.

Trump Says Ukraine ‘Has to Want to Make a Deal’ as Witkoff Heads to Russia — Speaking to reporters at the White House on Tuesday, Oct. 20, US President Donald Trump said Ukraine must want to make a deal and claimed that Washington received nothing in return for its aid, despite Kyiv repeatedly backing ceasefire proposals. His remarks came as President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed US intelligence sharing had resumed following talks with senior US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, Norway.

US Restores Intelligence to Ukraine as Witkoff Carries Peace Proposals to Putin — US intelligence sharing with Ukraine has resumed after a week of missed allied ballistic missile warnings, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday, Oct. 20, following talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, Norway. Witkoff is set to present proposals discussed there to Russia’s leadership in St. Petersburg, with security guarantees on the table, while Zelensky expects results on Patriot interceptors and Sta

Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region Over 70 Times, Killing 2, Wounding 7 — Russian forces struck four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region over 70 times on Tuesday, Oct. 20, killing two men and injuring seven people. According to the Head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, Oleksandr Hanzha, the casualties came in a strike on warehouses near Dnipro, while drone and artillery fire also hit the Synelynkove, Nikopol and Kryvyi Rih districts.

Japan Lifts 5-Year Restrictions on Ukrainian Poultry, Egg Imports — Japan has resumed imports of Ukrainian poultry, eggs and egg products after five years of import restrictions, Ukraine’s ambassador to Japan Yurii Lutovinov said on Monday, Oct. 19. The decision was formally agreed upon on Oct. 16, and it opens a new market for Ukrainian producers, while adding to growing cooperation between Kyiv and Tokyo.

Russia Hits Kyiv Cardiology Institute’s Operating Room — Russian forces struck an operating room in Kyiv’s Strazhesko Institute of Cardiology on Tuesday, Oct. 20, injuring one patient, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said. The strike marks the second time Russia targeted the heart center that serves patients nationwide, after a September 2025 strike killed two people there.

Russian Drones Hit Kyiv Medical Facilities in Daytime Raid — Russian drones struck Kyiv Tuesday afternoon, damaging medical facilities and scattering debris across several districts. The city’s military administration reported five people injured by 5 p.m., with the attack still underway. The Kyiv City Council denied reports that the North Bridge itself had been hit, while warning of traffic disruption near the crossing.

North Korea Shares ‘Proof of Life’ Photos Over Death Rumors of Kim Jong Un — Social media rumors that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un had died after suffering a brain hemorrhage were picked up by the international press. In response, Pyongyang’s state media reported on a visit with his daughter to a clothing and footwear exhibition.

Kallas Says US Negotiators Tried to Push Ukraine Into Surrender for 1.5 Years — EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused US negotiators of trying to push Ukraine into surrendering to Russia for around 1.5 years. She called for Europe's involvement in peace talks, tougher pressure on Moscow and a just, lasting settlement.

Romanian Parliament Approves Pro-EU Govt After Months of Deadlock — Romania’s parliament approved Luca Niculescu’s pro-European government with 280 votes, ending months of political deadlock. Backed by the Social Democrats, liberals and UDMR, the cabinet faces tensions between party ministers and technocrats, while the far-right AUR opposes the government.

Hungary Blocks Ukraine’s Next EU Step Despite Reset – Report — Hungary refused to approve a procedural step toward opening Ukraine’s final two EU negotiating clusters, European Pravda reported, citing diplomats. The reported objection follows last week’s breakthrough on two other clusters and talks aimed at rebuilding Kyiv-Budapest relations. Ukraine and Ireland’s EU presidency aim to open the remaining clusters before the end of 2026.

Russia Resumes Diesel Exports to Turkey, Brazil Despite Export Ban — Reuters said Russia has resumed diesel shipments to its major buyers following Trump’s diesel deal, with one tanker departing for Turkey on Oct. 14 and another for Brazil two days later, around the time Kyiv resumed its refinery attacks. Trump previously suggested Russia would export up to 2 million tons of diesel to the world market by year-end, while Moscow later boasted of 3.5 million.

Kyiv-Chelm Train – One Reporter’s Experience — On Oct 16-17, a Kyiv Post reporter rode a train from Kyiv’s main rail station to Chelm Poland, a popular destination for connection trains for people travelling from Ukraine to Warsaw and other cities in Poland. While Russian attacks have slowed down Ukrainian trains, they have not stopped them.

Lavrov Claims Peace Deal Would Mean End of Zelensky’s ‘Regime’ — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov accused Zelensky of repeatedly derailing peace negotiations, citing the Minsk process, Istanbul talks and trilateral meetings in Abu Dhabi. He added Ukraine undermined US-backed diplomatic efforts and alleged that any agreement acceptable to Moscow and Washington would mean the end of Zelensky’s “regime” and “of him personally.”

Zelensky Lands in Norway for Peace Talks With Trump’s Envoy — President Volodymyr Zelensky has arrived in Norway for talks with US envoy Steve Witkoff, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb. His agenda includes separate and joint meetings focused on peace efforts, stronger air defenses and joint production. Trump envoy Jared Kushner will participate remotely, while Zelensky will also meet Norway’s king and parliamentary leaders.

Slovenian Company Unveils Anti-Drone System Based on War-Proven Turret in Ukraine — The Slovenian remote-controlled weapon station (RCWS) specialist Valhalla Turrets has introduced the “Skythunder” counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS). Based on the success of the MANGART 25 in Ukraine, its use of critical US components suggests it was designed to compete for the Pentagon’s C-UAS program.

France Flails — France’s escalating protests expose a deepening clash over welfare spending, public debt and generational priorities. Diane Francis argues that the country’s fiscal crisis could destabilize the EU, unsettle financial markets and threaten Europe’s ability to sustain support for Ukraine.

US Intel Still Flows But Missile Warnings May Lag, Zelensky Advisor Says — Presidential adviser Beskrestnov says that US intelligence continues to reach Ukraine, but warnings of Russian missile attacks can arrive just a minute before impact. He also said Starlink and Starshield restrictions remain in place and that Kyiv is exploring alternatives for military communications, air defense and civilian connectivity.

Trust in Zelensky Rises to 57% After US Pressure, Poll Finds — A new Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KIIS) poll found that 57% of respondents trusted President Volodymyr Zelensky in interviews conducted Oct. 10-16, up from 43% in a smaller group surveyed on Oct. 8-9. KIIS said the increase likely reflects a “rally-around-the-flag” effect after the US-Russia diesel deal and pressure on Ukraine. In the overall October survey, 54% said they trusted Zelensky and 41% did not.

EU Considers Restricted Schengen Visas for Russian Tourists — The EU is considering broader use of territorially restricted visas for Russian tourists amid security concerns. The plan has been under discussion since summer 2026, with France and Italy reportedly opposing a broader ban. In 2025, the total number of Schengen tourist visas issued reached a record 477,878.
CARTOON: The Ghost of True Republicanism Haunts Today’s Imposter — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Europe Needs to Follow Zelensky’s Lead in Challenging Washington’s Appeasement — Tim Ash argues that a potential Trump-Putin-Xi summit could sideline Ukraine and Europe, revive great-power spheres of influence and reward Russia’s aggression. He warns that appeasing Putin will prolong the war and urges Europe to confront Washington and strengthen its support for Kyiv.

First War Death Reported in Putin's Hometown After Kyiv's Record Drone Assault — Russian media reported the death of a taxi driver in St. Petersburg during Ukraine’s Sunday record drone attack on the city and surrounding region. Reports say the death marked the first civilian death in the city over four years into Russia’s invasion, while the UN warned that confirmed civilian casualties in Ukraine spiked 55 percent year-on-year to 15,280 within just the first eight months of 2026, with local aut

An Unhappy Republic: France’s Troubles Extend Beyond the Street — France’s protests over rising living costs, deteriorating public services and political frustration are exposing deep divisions ahead of next year’s presidential election, strengthening anti-establishment forces and raising concerns that unrest could spread across Europe.

Witkoff to Meet Zelensky, European Leaders in Oslo Before Moscow Trip — Steve Witkoff is due to meet Zelensky and European leaders to develop peace proposals ahead of a planned Russia visit, as Kyiv seeks security guarantees and continued US military support.

Zelensky Raises Issues of Missile Defense, Warnings, Starlink with Rubio — Zelensky said he discussed ballistic missile interceptors, early warning systems for Russian attacks, and restoring Starlink/Starshield availability with US Secretary of State Rubio. The two agreed to speak again as diplomatic efforts to end Russia’s war continue.

US to Convert Sanctioned Oil Tankers Into Legal Shipping Fleet, Energy Secretary Says — The Trump administration plans to convert sanctioned oil tankers into legitimate commercial vessels to ease a global shipping crunch triggered by the war in Iran. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright also defended efforts to release Russian diesel supplies onto global markets, saying they could incentivize Moscow to end its war against Ukraine.

Poland Scrambles Aircraft Twice Amid Russian Attacks on Ukraine — Poland scrambled military aircraft twice on Oct. 18 as Russia carried out air attacks on Ukraine, with alerts sent to residents of the Lublin and Subcarpathian regions. The alerts were lifted after the threat passed. The deployments came as Russian forces attacked western Ukraine, including a drone strike near Lviv that set a warehouse building on fire.

Russia Claims 136 Ukrainian Drones Downed, Hits on Druzhba Pipeline Facility — A fire was reported at the Nikolskoye station in Russia’s Tambov region after monitoring channels and Astra reported a drone attack. Russia claimed it downed 136 Ukrainian drones overnight, while Astra reported damage to a major building in occupied Donetsk.

Russian Drone Strike Near Kyiv-Odesa Highway Kills 3 — A Russian drone strike near the Kyiv-Odesa highway in Chabany killed three people and injured four on Tuesday, according to preliminary information from authorities. Cars caught fire near a shopping center, and traffic was restricted on the affected stretch. Investigators and emergency services were working at the scene as authorities clarified the number of casualties.

South Korea to Withdraw More Embassy Staff From Ukraine Amid North Korean POW Dispute — South Korea will withdraw some staff from its embassy in Ukraine as a diplomatic dispute escalates over Kyiv’s disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul, despite Ukraine’s insistence that the matter has been resolved.

Zelensky Accuses US of Delaying Patriot Missiles as Tensions With Trump Grow — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the Pentagon of delaying Patriot missile deliveries already paid for by European allies, saying the weapons were awaiting US approval. The dispute comes as Kyiv faces renewed Russian strikes and growing tensions with Washington over military aid and intelligence sharing.

Russian State TV Downplays Ukraine’s Biggest Drone Attack on St. Petersburg, Focuses on France Protests — Russian state TV largely ignored Ukraine’s biggest drone attack of the war on St. Petersburg, devoting more airtime to protests in France than to strikes that damaged oil infrastructure, a logistics center and a data center, the BBC’s Russian Service reported.

1 Week Without US Intelligence: Russian Ballistics Kill At Least 6 Ukrainians, 21 Injured — Following the US cut-off of ballistic missile early-warning intelligence to Ukraine, Russian ballistic missile strikes have killed at least six civilians and left more than 20 injured. US officials deny there has been a cut-off, but Ukrainian officials, military sources, media outlets, and civilian air-defense networks agree that Russian ballistic missiles are now hitting targets before launch warnings ar

‘Almost No Patriot Missiles Left’ – Zelensky Offers 30-Day Pause on Russian Oil Strikes in Exchange for US Interceptors — Zelensky says Ukraine has nearly exhausted its US-supplied Patriot interceptors and offered to halt Russian refinery strikes for 30 days in exchange for US air defense assistance.

Russia Strikes Ukrainian Energy Facility, Damages Church in Overnight Drone Attacks – 2 Killed in Khmelnytsky — Russian drones struck an energy facility twice in Lviv region and damaged a church and industrial site in Khmelnytsky, where an earlier attack killed two women.

‘Trump May Trade Ukraine for Putin’s Help on Iran’ – Ex-NATO Commander Warns of ‘Corrupt, Dangerous Bargain’ — Former NATO commander Wesley Clark accused Trump of potentially sacrificing Ukraine to secure Putin’s cooperation on Iran, comparing the possible deal to the 1938 Munich Agreement, when Hitler was appeased after invading Czechoslovakia.

‘Trump Has Been Putin’s Puppet’ – US Congresswoman Slams White House Over Ukraine Aid Delays — Congresswoman Madeleine Dean accused Trump of helping Putin by delaying $400 million in weapons for Ukraine, disrupting missile warnings, and easing sanctions on Russia.

Trump Open to Meeting Putin and Xi Without Zelensky, Says Ukraine Needs New Negotiator — Trump says he is willing to meet Putin and Xi in China, defends easing sanctions on Russia and suggests someone else should negotiate for Ukraine, drawing objections from Kyiv.

Pope Leo XIV Calls Zelensky After Speaking With Putin to Discuss Russian-Occupied Oleshky Again — Pope Leo XIV spoke with Zelensky three days after appealing to Putin for a humanitarian ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where civilians face severe shortages of food and medicine.

Zelensky Tells US Lawmakers Washington Has Yet to Explain Starlink Limits, Missed Missile Warnings — Speaking during a virtual meeting on Monday, Oct. 19, President Volodymyr Zelensky told a bipartisan group of US lawmakers that Washington has yet to explain the Starlink speed limits or the missing warnings of Russian ballistic missile attacks. On the same day, he also met with the team of the American defense company, Lockheed Martin, in Kyiv, as Ukraine seeks more Patriot interceptors that it

Russian Strikes Kill 2 in Kryvyi Rih as Dnipropetrovsk Region Braces for Winter Blackouts — Russian forces struck the Dnipropetrovsk region over 20 times with drones and artillery on Monday, Oct. 19, killing two people and injuring 10, including a 15-year-old boy. The attacks came as regional authorities continue preparing for the upcoming winter and possible power outages by adding more than 125 megawatts (MW) of alternative generation this year to keep heat and water running.

Bulgaria Seeks Arrest of 2 German Nationals Over Arson Attack on Starlink Antennas — Bulgaria has issued European arrest warrants for two German nationals aged 19, accused of burning eight Starlink antennas near Sofia. The case adds to a string of suspected sabotage attacks on Starlink infrastructure in Europe, particularly in Poland and Lithuania, as authorities warn that Russia could increase its hybrid warfare and sabotage campaigns across the continent in the upcoming months.

Russia Strikes Ecosoft, Planeta Plastic With Ballistic Missiles — Russian ballistic missiles struck the facilities of water purification company Ecosoft and polymer manufacturer Planeta Plastic overnight Oct. 18-19. The strikes formed part of a massive attack involving 16 missiles and over 200 drones targeting Ukrainian infrastructure.

Republican Congressman Threatens Trump Administration Over Ukraine’s Starshield Limits — US Representative Brian Fitzpatrick, a Pennsylvania Republican, has vowed investigations, public hearings and budget cuts for anyone who restricted Ukraine’s Starshield access. President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed on Monday, Oct. 19, that Starlink terminals still fail above 130-161 km/h (81-100 mph), although US President Donald Trump previously denied ordering restrictions, and claimed the system operated

Kyiv Metro to Resume Full Service Past Damaged Chernihivska Station — Kyiv is planning to restore a full metro service between Lisova and Akademmistechko on the evening of Monday, Oct. 19, with trains bypassing the damaged Chernihivska station. To offset the disruption, the capital has added 15 buses along the routes - No. 1-M and 118, Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said.

Infant Dies in Stroller as Russian Drone Kills 6, Including 2 Children, in Kharkiv Park — Russian forces struck a crowded park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv region with a drone on Monday, Oct. 19, killing six people, including three children. Among them, an infant was killed in a stroller. Fourteen people, including seven children, were wounded. Prosecutors have opened a war crimes investigation into the attack, as deliberately targeting civilians constitutes a violation of international humanitaria

New Survey Shows 61% of Ukrainians Oppose Land for Peace Deal — Most Ukrainians reject ceding all of Donbas in exchange for security guarantees, while 35% would accept the concession. Opposition spans every region.

‘Russia Is a Global Problem, Not a Powerʼ: Sybiha Reacts to Trilateral Proposal Without Ukraine — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said a meeting between the leaders of Ukraine, the US and Russia could help end the war, while a Trump-Xi-Putin summit could encourage the Kremlin to continue it. His comments follow reports that Putin proposed meeting the US and Chinese presidents in November to discuss the war. Kyiv has also backed a separate trilateral format that would include Ukraine.

500 Wagner Fighters, $400M a Year – Prigozhin’s Son Holds On to His African Empire — Pavel Prigozhin, the son of Wagner founder Yevgeny Prigozhin, has reportedly kept the group’s military presence and expanded its business interests in the CAR, where about 500 operatives remain deployed. The group’s mining concessions and security partnership with President Touadéra have helped it resist Moscow’s Africa Corps takeover efforts

Russia Hits 28 Substations in Overnight Strike, Zelensky Says — The Ukrainian president said Russia’s overnight strike on Monday across Ukraine damaged 28 substations and unnamed facilities, cutting power to at least 550,000 households. He said earlier that Kyiv was not forewarned of the 16 ballistic missiles Russia launched towards Ukraine despite the supposedly restored intelligence flow from Washington.

Russia Attempts to Cut Kyiv Water Supply, Kremlin Documents Show — Prime Minister Koretskyi said Russia is increasingly focusing on Kyiv’s water supply and urged residents to prepare for difficult conditions this winter. Russian attacks continue to damage energy infrastructure: Kyiv’s three main combined heat and power plants stopped generating electricity, and a recent nationwide attack damaged more than 10 energy facilities and left at least 550,000 households without power.

Europe Weighs More Ukraine Support as Trump Waives Sanctions — Ukraine reported another Russian ballistic attack without prior warnings on Monday, Oct. 19, despite Zelensky’s announcement that US intelligence sharing had resumed. European governments are preparing further sanctions and weapons supplies, but additional financing remains unresolved.

Beijing Says No Info on Rumored Trump, Xi, Putin Trilateral Talks — Beijing said on Monday that it has no information about a planned trilateral summit between the leaders of the US, China and Russia. Putin reportedly proposed the summit during a call with Trump on Oct. 9, before Trump announced a diesel deal with Moscow, with Secretary of State Rubio confirming that discussions for the summit are ongoing but not finalized.

Wounded Ukrainian Soldier Airlifted by Heavy Drone in World’s First — The Ukrainian military evacuated a wounded infantryman from his position using a heavy hexacopter, in an operation involving multiple brigades and the drone’s manufacturer. A brigade involved said ground robots could not be used because of heavy Russian drone activity and mined routes, with the wounded soldier now receiving medical care after his rescue.

Trump’s Policies Upping the Pressure on Zelensky — Donald Trump faces mounting European criticism for policies seen as favouring Russia, including a diesel deal with Vladimir Putin, calls for Ukraine to stop attacking Russian refineries, and the abandonment of new sanctions against Moscow. While critics warn this could weaken Western unity and harm Ukraine, others argue Europe’s failure to provide sufficient military support is prolonging the war without a realistic path to victory.

Russia Rebuilds Military Stockpiles Near NATO Borders — Russia is replenishing military equipment at storage bases across the country, including sites around 310 miles from Estonia and Latvia and 115 miles from Finland, according to satellite imagery analyzed by OSINT researchers. The equipment includes newly built T-90M tanks and artillery systems, as well as refurbished vehicles. Researchers stress that the vehicles remain at storage bases and have not been transferred to active units.

The couple have a four-year-old daughter, Skai.
